ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-008", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Additional rules: choose the category that the evidence about the cause supports, not the one the symptoms suggest. downstream_timeout needs evidence that the dependency itself is slow or that calls to it timed out. Cite the evidence that identifies the cause (the telltale log line or the metric that changed), not only symptom lines.

Step 6: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "bad deployment rolling back new release mitigation steps"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook for bad deployment to get mitigation steps.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-01-5 (similarity 0.68).
  [R-01-5] Bad deployment or regression - Mitigation (similarity 0.68): Go back to the previous release straight away by redeploying the last version known to be good. Do not spend time debugging on the live service first. Pause any further releases to this service until the cause is understood and a fix has been reviewed and tested.
  [R-01-3] Bad deployment or regression - How to confirm (similarity 0.67): Line the start of the trouble up against the release timeline. If it began just after a rollout and the previous version was healthy, suspect the release. Look at what the service wrote to its logs while the new version was starting and when the first failures arrived, and compare with an older instance if one is still running.
  [R-01-2] Bad deployment or regression - Symptoms (similarity 0.64): Things go wrong shortly after a rollout. Customers start seeing failures, dashboards turn red around the time the new version went out, and the problem does not fade by itself. The service may also restart a few times while the new version rolls through.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- misconfiguration: Logs explicitly show startup validation failing and requests being rejected due to an invalid configuration parameter (FEATURE_NEW_PRICING='true'), coinciding with restarts and the error rate spike. (evidence: M-032, M-036, L-0274, L-0276)
- bad_deployment: Service restarts and failures occurring right after startup indicate a problematic deployment or configuration release causing service instability. (evidence: M-032, M-036, L-0274)
- downstream_timeout: Some logs mention upstream/downstream returning 503 errors, though configuration issues appear more primary. (evidence: M-032, L-0284)
